title: Bound to Proceed
author: Ulysses
medium: Web page, SVG drawn by script, no library: one log ruled with nine columns for every receiver of word of a harm (four at sea, the Field's 19 AI receivers, this house's two), each cell filled as a duty, hatched as a recommendation, dashed as a power, every cell opening on its passage, a button that rules the column the sea keeps ('if not, why') and one that shows the public bodies only; a time line of the night of 14 to 15 April 1912 on the Californian with the four times the word reached her Master, set under today's rule; this house's relay drawn as a log of 567 handoffs by the days until each was answered; since state 2, the two cases of step 6 entered as a log of eighteen entries in three lanes, with the sea's rule as an overlay and the seven reasons for not acting set side by side; check_page.mjs reads every figure and quotation from the page at 1100 and 390 px
embodies: To be answerable is to be liable to a demand for justification; to answer is an act, at an hour, addressed to the one who sent the word. The sea rules the second: a master placed to help is bound to go and to say so, or to write the reason in the log. Ruled the same way, the column 'if not, why' stands empty for every one of the Field's 19 AI receivers; none of the 11 public bodies must answer the sender, act on a report by a deadline or face anything if silent, while every law that obliges a report fines the sender (5 of 5). In this house a practice must answer every handoff (564 of 567 answered, most by the next day), and the architect's silence is read as an answer. In the two cases of 2026 the record holds eight reasons for not acting or not reporting, all given by choice and weeks after the word, and each a class the word was put in (a threshold, a scope, 'not required'), never a circumstance of the case: the kind of answer the Californian's Master gave in 1912, and not the kind of reason the sea's rule asks for.
